$comment: WHAT EVERY PUBLISHED ASSET MUST CONTAIN — the list, in one place, read by two readers.
Written 2026-09-22, after v2.12.0 shipped with two of its headline claims untrue of the
zips people downloaded. That release was the one that found four runtime payloads staged
into $(OutDir) and never into the publish, and it fixed the MSBuild correctly. But two of
the four are third-party binaries that are not in the repository, every item is Exists()-
guarded so a build without them succeeds in silence, and the release is built by GitHub
Actions, which did not have them. The fix landed on one machine and not on the artifact.
PublishStagingParityTests cannot catch that and is not at fault: parsing the csproj as XML
verifies the RULES, and whether the file exists on the release runner is a different
question that no test reading this repository can answer. The check has to be on the
artifact. scripts/verify_release_payloads.py applies this file to the built zips inside the
release job, before anything is published.
The same file is read by ReleasePayloadManifestTests, which asserts that everything named
here is also staged by the csproj that owns it — so the two halves cannot drift: a payload
added to the build without being added to the artifact check, or vice versa, is a test
failure rather than a discovery made by reading a published zip six months later.

required.why: without it PluginTrustPolicy.RequireTrusted enforces an empty allow-list and refuses all 33 plugin DLLs — the market dropdown offers only the built-in providers, with nothing saying why
the provider and analytics plugins the manifest above vouches for
RoslynScriptingService resolves the worker from AppContext.BaseDirectory and Release refuses the in-process path by design, so without the exe no user-compiled indicator or strategy can run at all

The parity test matches on the project name the wildcard is rooted at; the ARTIFACT check still demands this exact file, which is the half that matters.

required.why: NVDA-direct speech. The chart is a native SkiaSharp canvas over the BlazorWebView, so a reader focused on the chart is not reading the DOM and the ARIA live-region fallback cannot reach it. NO DLL MEANS THE CHART IS SILENT — which is the whole application. NV Access renamed the file, so either spelling counts.

the tactile SDK entry point WindowsDotPadNative binds its exports on; absent, the driver logs 'NativeLibrary.TryLoad failed ... Tactile DISABLED' and falls back to NullDotPadNative while the Braille tab keeps rendering, which is the worst of the two
the braille translator behind DOT_PAD_BRAILLE_DISPLAY. The SDK LoadLibrary's it by name and reports DOT_ERROR_LIBLOUIS_DLL_COULD_NOT_LOAD when it is missing.

the LibLouis translation tables. The SDK calls lou_setDataPath at a \tables directory beside itself and names 35 specific .ctb/.utb files; without them there is no text-to-braille. 419 files at 3.0.0.
the SDK's text-to-braille engine, LoadLibrary'd by DotPadSDK at runtime
a STATIC import of TTBEngine.dll — read out of its PE import table, so TTBEngine cannot load without it beside it
a Dot Pad SDK module its siblings expect beside them
the MeCab config the SDK reads at init

DotPadSDK-3.0.0.dll STATICALLY imports MSVCP140/VCRUNTIME140/VCRUNTIME140_1 — read out of its PE import table. A .NET publish carries none of them, so on a machine without the VC++ 2015-2022 redistributable NativeLibrary.TryLoad fails and tactile is silently disabled: the exact symptom shipping the SDK is meant to end.
see msvcp140.dll
see msvcp140.dll

why: ADVISORY, NOT BLOCKING, and honestly so: as of the v2.12.0 re-cut this is NOT FIXED.
v2.11.0's Windows app was precompiled and v2.12.0's was not, with nothing in the repo
setting PublishReadyToRun either way — an implicit default moved under us. Confirmed by
reading the CLI header's ManagedNativeHeader out of both published zips: non-empty in
2.11.0, zero in 2.12.0. It costs startup and first-use JIT on the head with the slowest
PublishReadyToRun=true is now set in the csproj under a condition that demonstrably
holds, and the artifact STILL comes out IL-only, so something in the MAUI/WinUI import
chain assigns it. Passing it as a command-line global property did not restore R2R
either, and it broke something real on the way: a global property flows into every
referenced project, the SDK inferred a RuntimeIdentifier for the ScriptWorker, and the
apphost ended up in publish/maui-win/win-x64/ instead of the root — a missing FEATURE,
So this reports and does not block. Every other rule in this file is about a feature
that is silently dead without it; this one is about how fast the app starts, and a
corrected release must not be held hostage to it. Turn severity back to 'fail' the day
the shipped bytes actually carry a ManagedNativeHeader.

runtimeconfig.why: the Windows app runs on the user's installed .NET; a runtimeconfig that accepts 10.0.0 starts it on an unpatched runtime (2.16.0 did). Cody 2026-11-28: require the pinned patch. PinShippedRuntime=true on the Windows publish sets it.

assets.head: the Windows download's own top folder

required.why: the one program at the top of the download; it starts app\AccessibleTrader.BlazorClient.exe. Without it the user unzips a folder holding only README.txt and app\, and has to find the right exe among 480 files and three exes, which is the problem this layout exists to end
says which file to run, that the app folder must stay beside it, and where settings live

$note: The installer, AccessibleTrader-<version>-Windows-Setup.exe, is built from the same staged
folder and is not read here: packaging/windows/package.ps1 installs it on the Windows runner
and compares every installed file with the staged one before the job can succeed.

assets.head: the MAUI macOS (Mac Catalyst) app

required.why: the published v2.12.0 .app carried 33 plugin DLLs in Contents/MonoBundle and no manifest. The publish-time target DID run — it wrote the manifest beside the bundle, into $(PublishDir), while the workflow zipped the bundle. A payload one directory outside the thing you ship is not shipped.
the plugins the manifest vouches for; AppContext.BaseDirectory is MonoBundle on this head, so both must be there

$note: No ScriptWorker here, and that is deliberate rather than an omission:
("macCatalyst"), so there is no external exe to stage. No NVDA or Dot Pad payload

runtime.why: The bundled .NET runtime must be the version Directory.Build.props pins (ShippedRuntimeVersion). 2.16.0 shipped runtime 10.0.11 in the WebHost zips and 10.0.0 in the Mac app, both older than the Brotli decoder fix in 10.0.14, because a self-contained publish bundles its SDK band's runtime unless PinShippedRuntime=true asks for another.
